FACTUAL MATRIX 1.

Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution against the accused is that on 13.03.2015 at about 03.00 PM in front of Reliance Fresh, Village Hassanpur, Delhi-52, while the complainant Tarun was crossing the road in front of Reliance Fresh, Village Hasanpur, Delhi, a truck/dumper bearing registration No. HR 55J 5688 approached in a rash and negligent manner and collided with his motorcycle, a Passion Pro bearing registration No. DL 7 SAE 6303.
As a result of the accident, his trousers were torn.
The driver of the truck allegedly ran the offending vehicle over the witness's leg twice, causing bleeding injuries.
An auto-rickshaw was standing behind the offending vehicle at the time of the incident and he transported him to Max Hospital in his vehicle.

As such, it is alleged that the accused committed the offence under sections 279/337 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC") for which FIR No. 908/2015 was registered at Police Station Madhu Vihar,
Delhi.

15. The gravamen of the offence under section 279 IPC is the act of accused, done with "rashness" or "negligence".
The IPC does not define either of these terms.
However, the ambit of these terms has now been settled by judicial pronouncements from time to time.

16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Rathnashavlvan vs. State of Karnataka (2007)
3 SCC 474 has observed, inter alia, as under:
"7. .... Culpable negligence lies in the failure to exercise reasonable and proper precautions and the extent of its reasonableness will always depend upon the circumstances of each case.

sentences.text: Rashness means doing an act with the consciousness of a risk that evil consequences will follow but with the hope that it will not.
Negligence is a breach of duty imposed by law.
In criminal cases, the amount and degree of negligence are determining factors.

A question whether the accused's conduct amounted to culpable rashness or negligence depends directly on the question as to what is the amount of precaution and circumspection which a prudent and reasonable man would consider it to be sufficient considering all the circumstances of the case.

Criminal rashness means hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is dangerous or wanton and the further knowledge that it may cause injury but done without any intention to cause injury or knowledge that it would probably be caused.
8. As noted above, "rashness" consists in hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so, and that it may cause injury.
The criminality lies in such a case in running the risk of doing such an act with recklessness or indifference as to the consequences.

Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard to all the Digitally signed by Udbhav Udbhav Kumar Jain Kumar Date:
FIR No. 908/2015 State vs. Luvkush Jain 2025.06.10 Page no. 12 of 17 17:56:01 +0530 circumstances out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted."
17.
Similar observations were made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushil Ansal vs. CBI (2014) 6 SCC 173.

The standard of negligence was discussed in the said case, by observing, inter alia,
as under: -
"58.

In the case of "negligence" the courts have favoured a meaning which implies a gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual which having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge arises, it may be State vs Luvkush on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92030256/
8 the imperative duty of the accused to have adopted.

Negligence has been understood to be an omission to do something which a reasonable man guided upon those considerations which ordinarily regulate the conduct of human affairs, would do, or doing something which a prudent and reasonable person would not do.

Unlike rashness, where the immutability arises from acting despite the consciousness,
negligence implies acting without such consciousness, but in circumstances which show that the actor has not exercised the caution incumbent upon him.
The immutability in the case of negligence arises from the neglect of the civil duty of circumspection."

18. In S.N. Hussain v. State of A.P., (1972) 3 SCC 18, the Hon'ble Supreme Court while discussing rashness and criminal negligence observed:
"9. ... Rashness consists in hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so, and that it may cause injury.

sentences.text: The general burden of proof, which is a non-shifting burden, on the prosecution is to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by adducing cogent evidence that point only towards the guilt of accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE AND REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE 21.

In totality four witnesses were examined by the prosecution and after going through the testimonies of all the witnesses, following are the issues/facts that have erupted which raise doubts on the version of prosecution:
a.
There is a delay of almost 6 months in lodging of FIR from the date of alleged incident and there is no reasonable or sufficient explanation for such inordinate delay in lodging of FIR.

c. Even the damaged vehicle was produced in the PS after almost 6 months which creates doubt on the version of the complainant as to whether the damage was caused to the vehicle on the date of alleged incident and whether the same was caused by the accused.

d. Neither the complainant provided any details of the auto- rickshaw driver who took him to hospital, nor the IO of the case took any steps to trace the said person even though he was a material witness in the present case.
e. No TIP of the accused was conducted rather the accused was identified by the complainant in the PS itself.
Why the complainant came to the PS on the date when accused produced before the IO is also questionable.
f. PW-1 has merely deposed that the accused was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, but it is not clear as to how the accused was driving the vehicle in such a manner.
Mere use of the words as provided in the provision does not make the accused guilty.
The presumption of innocence is in favour of the accused and for it to be rebutted, cogent evidence has to be led.

g. It is not the case that the alleged incident took place behind closed doors and when the same was committed on a public road then why no public person who saw the alleged incident was neither examined nor made as a witness created adverse inference on the story of the prosecution itself.

Reliance here is also placed upon illustration (g) to Section 114 of the Evidence Act, 1872.
h.
There is no evidence in particular which connects the accused with alleged commission of offences.

Due to the issues/facts as pointed out above, it cannot be said that the prosecution is successful in bringing home the guilt of accused.
It cannot be said without a reasonable doubt that accused was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
In fact, presence of the accused on the spot is also doubtful.
Further nothing has come on record especially from the testimony of PW-1 that the accused was driving the vehicle recklessly or indifferently as to the consequences.

Criminal negligence to the extent of gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular is also missing and has not been proved.

Mere statement by PW-1 that the accused was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner does not prove that that accused had the required intent or his conduct was such that the ingredients of the offence are satisfied.

Reliance here is placed upon the judgement passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyam vs State Of Andhra Pradesh AIR 2000 SC 2511.

The nature of burden of proof to prove the guilt of accused is beyond reasonable doubt but the accused has been successful in raising doubt on the version of prosecution which implies that prosecution has not been able to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.

24. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in S.L. Goswami (Dr) v. State of M.P., (1972) 3 SCC 22 held that the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence is not discharged by the prosecution.

opennyai_summary.facts:
An auto-rickshaw was standing behind the offending vehicle at the time of the incident and he transported him to Max Hospital in his vehicle.
After registration of FIR, the investigating officer (hereinafter 'IO') conducted investigation and during investigation it was found that the person namely Luvkush was driving the offending vehicle and the nature of injury suffered by the complainant/victim was grievous in nature.
On culmination of the investigation, chargesheet against the present accused namely Luvkush for the alleged commission of offences u/s 279/338 IPC was filed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
While the first, second and third ingredient needs to be established beyond reasonable doubt with the aid of direct and circumstantial evidence, the Digitally signed by Udbhav Udbhav Kumar Jain Kumar Date:
Criminal rashness means hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is dangerous or wanton and the further knowledge that it may cause injury but done without any intention to cause injury or knowledge that it would probably be caused.
The criminality lies in such a case in running the risk of doing such an act with recklessness or indifference as to the consequences.
Digitally signed by Udbhav Udbhav Jain Kumar FIR No. 908/2015 State vs. Luvkush Kumar Date: Page no. 13 of 17 Jain 2025.06.10 17:56:09 +0530 precautions that a person placed in the effect situation ought to take, in order to avoid injuries.
20.
The general burden of proof, which is a non-shifting burden, on the prosecution is to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The presumption of innocence of the accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by adducing cogent evidence that point only towards the guilt of accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE AND REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE 21.
In totality four witnesses were examined by the prosecution and after going through the testimonies of all the witnesses, following are the issues/facts that have erupted which raise doubts on the version of prosecution:
a.
There is a delay of almost 6 months in lodging of FIR from the date of alleged incident and there is no reasonable or sufficient explanation for such inordinate delay in lodging of FIR.
Thus, the lodging of FIR is clearly an afterthought.
c. Even the damaged vehicle was produced in the PS after almost 6 months which creates doubt on the version of the complainant as to whether the damage was caused to the vehicle on the date of alleged incident and whether the same was caused by the accused.
f. PW-1 has merely deposed that the accused was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, but it is not clear as to how the accused was driving the vehicle in such a manner.
Mere use of the words as provided in the provision does not make the accused guilty.
The presumption of innocence is in favour of the accused and for it to be rebutted, cogent evidence has to be led.
g. It is not the case that the alleged incident took place behind closed doors and when the same was committed on a public road then why no public person who saw the alleged incident was neither examined nor made as a witness created adverse inference on the story of the prosecution itself.
There is no evidence in particular which connects the accused with alleged commission of offences.
Due to the issues/facts as pointed out above, it cannot be said that the prosecution is successful in bringing home the guilt of accused.
It cannot be said without a reasonable doubt that accused was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
In fact, presence of the accused on the spot is also doubtful.
Further nothing has come on record especially from the testimony of PW-1 that the accused was driving the vehicle recklessly or indifferently as to the consequences.
Criminal negligence to the extent of gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular is also missing and has not been proved.
Mere statement by PW-1 that the accused was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner does not prove that that accused had the required intent or his conduct was such that the ingredients of the offence are satisfied.
Reliance here is placed upon the judgement passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyam vs State Of Andhra Pradesh AIR 2000 SC 2511.
23.
Thus, there are material contradictions in the case of prosecution which are fatal to the case of prosecution itself.
The nature of burden of proof to prove the guilt of accused is beyond reasonable doubt but the accused has been successful in raising doubt on the version of prosecution which implies that prosecution has not been able to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
24. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in S.L. Goswami (Dr) v. State of M.P., (1972) 3 SCC 22 held that the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence is not discharged by the prosecution.
In the present case, as already noted above, the prosecution could not discharge the burden of proving the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Thus, accused Luvkush is entitled to benefit of doubt.
